structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, the membrane surface of normal biconcave red cells reconstructed in 3D has a mean curvature that varies substantially across the surface (not constant), and the same cells in hypotonic suspension become near-spherical.
structured_output.pass_criterion: In at least 90% of segmented isotonic discocytes (n >= 100), the coefficient of variation of mean curvature H over the surface (excluding the rim) exceeds 0.5, and median sphericity of cells in hypotonic medium exceeds 0.95 versus below 0.80 in isotonic medium.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Refuted if the coefficient of variation of mean curvature over the surface is 0.2 or less in at least 50% of isotonic discocytes (a surface of near-constant mean curvature within measurement error), or if hypotonic cells do not become more spherical (median sphericity increase of 0.05 or less).
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'surface of equilibrium' under surface tension alone means a surface of constant mean curvature (a Delaunay or Plateau surface) at fixed pressure difference. 'Diluted blood' is mapped to hypotonic buffer. Modern caveat: real membranes have bending rigidity and a spectrin cytoskeleton, so the measurable test is whether mean curvature is constant. It is not whether a bending-energy model fits. The test bears on the 'surface tension alone' part of the claim, not on Thompson's speculation about the alternative cause (osmotic inequilibrium or fluid-crystal forces), which is not tested here.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: I could not find and verify a public deposit of 3D red-cell shape reconstructions (holotomography or similar) that includes both isotonic and hypotonic conditions and has a landing page and DOI I can confirm. One search turned up only journal articles on red-cell holotomography and an unrelated organoid dataset. Two-dimensional smear images cannot give mean curvature. I am reporting null rather than naming an unverified identifier. The test could be run if a verified deposit of 3D RBC tomograms with osmotic conditions is identified.
